• Avoid jargon and keep spoken sentences simple. Be prepared to give the interpreter different
or more explicit explanations of certain words and concepts, so that they can be translated.
• It is useful to provide the interpreter with a list of jargon and key concepts (eg “mitigation”,
“settlement”) in advance.
• Do not be surprised if the interpretation takes longer or less time than what was said in
English. That is because of the differences in how the languages work. The Advocate’s
